items.stem: To find the force pulling the block down the slope, the weight W should be resolved into components

options.text: along the slope and at right angles to the slope

misconception.label: The weight is already vertical, so resolving that way gains nothing.
A single component is not enough; the two together have to add back to W.

options.text: at right angles to the slope only

misconception.label: The perpendicular component presses the block into the slope and does not move it down.

steps: Choose axes that match the motion being considered.
The block can only slide along the slope, so one axis runs down the slope.
The other is at right angles to it, and that component is balanced by the push of the surface. The component along the slope is the one that would make the block slide.
solution.answer_line: along the slope and at right angles to the slope

items.stem: The block does not sink into the surface because the plane exerts on it a force that is

options.text: vertically upwards and equal to W

misconception.label: That would be true on level ground, but on a slope the reaction is not vertical and is smaller than W.

options.text: at right angles to the surface of the plane

misconception.label: Friction acts along the slope; the reaction does not.

Outwards from a surface means at right angles to it, which is why it is called the normal reaction.

items.stem: A dam is built thicker at the bottom than at the top because the water pressure

options.text: acts only sideways near the surface

misconception.label: Pressure acts equally in all directions at every depth.

steps: The pressure at depth h in a liquid is p = ρgh.
The deeper the point, the greater the weight of water above it and the larger the pressure.
So the outward push on the wall is greatest at the base, and the dam is built thickest there.

items.stem: A vibrating loudspeaker cone produces sound in air by

items.stem: The fuse in a plug is fitted in the live side rather than the neutral side so that when it blows

misconception.label: The earth connection is separate and is unaffected either way.

options.text: the neutral wire is protected from overheating

misconception.label: The neutral wire is the same size as the live and is not the thing at risk.

options.text: the current can still return to the supply

misconception.label: When the fuse blows no current flows at all, by design.

options.text: the appliance is cut off from the dangerous side of the supply

steps: A fuse anywhere in the loop will stop the current when it blows.
The question is what is left connected afterwards.
With the fuse in the live side, the break isolates the appliance from the live supply. With it in the neutral side, the appliance would still be joined to the live wire and dangerous to touch.
solution.answer_line: the appliance is cut off from the dangerous side of the supply

items.objective_statement: recall the symbols for AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR logic gates
items.stem: A logic gate drawn as a D shape with a small circle on its output is a

misconception.label: A NOT gate is a triangle with a circle, and it has only one input.
An OR gate has a curved back and a pointed nose, and no circle.
A NOR gate is the OR shape with a circle, not the D shape.

steps: Learn the two basic shapes: the D shape is AND, the curved and pointed shape is OR.
A small circle on the output means the output is inverted.
D shape plus circle is therefore NOT AND, which is NAND.

items.objective_statement: state the function of each gate with the aid of truth tables
items.stem: A NOT gate differs from the other basic gates in that it has

misconception.label: Every basic gate has a single output.
It has one input, not three.
It certainly has an output; that is the inverted input.

steps: AND, OR, NAND and NOR all combine at least two inputs into one output.
The NOT gate has nothing to combine; it just reverses what it is given.
So it takes one input and produces one output, and it is often called an inverter.

items.stem: Magnetic field lines are drawn closer together where the field is

misconception.label: Widely spaced lines show a weak field.

steps: Field lines are a way of picturing both direction and strength.

items.objective_statement: describe a commercial application of an electromagnet
items.stem: In an electric bell, the hammer strikes the gong repeatedly because the circuit

misconception.label: A bell works perfectly well on the direct current from a cell.

options.text: is broken by the moving armature and then made again

misconception.label: Heating plays no part in the action.

steps: Closing the switch energises the electromagnet, which pulls the armature over and the hammer strikes.
The moving armature opens a contact in the same circuit.
The electromagnet loses its magnetism, a spring pulls the armature back, the contact closes, and the cycle repeats.

items.objective_statement: explain the principle of operation of a transformer
items.stem: The soft iron core of a transformer is laminated in order to

misconception.label: The saving in mass is incidental and not the reason.
The turns ratio decides the voltage, not the lamination.

options.text: reduce the energy wasted by currents induced in the core
insulate the primary from the secondary

misconception.label: The windings are insulated by their own coating; the lamination is not for that.

steps: The alternating flux in the core induces e.m.f.s in the iron itself.
In a solid core these drive large eddy currents that heat it and waste energy.
Thin sheets separated by insulating varnish break up the paths for those currents, so much less energy is lost.
solution.answer_line: reduce the energy wasted by currents induced in the core

items.stem: Thomson's discovery that cathode rays are deflected by an electric field showed that the particles in them are

misconception.label: An uncharged particle would pass straight through the field.

steps: Cathode rays were passed between two charged plates.
They were deflected towards the positive plate.
Unlike charges attract, so the particles must be negative. Their deflection also showed they were far lighter than any atom.

items.objective_statement: describe the Geiger- Marsden experiment
items.stem: In the Geiger-Marsden experiment, the fact that most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil showed that an atom is

misconception.label: A solid atom would have stopped or deflected every particle.
The atom also contains electrons, and the experiment showed the positive charge is concentrated in a tiny volume.

steps: Alpha particles were fired at a foil only a few atoms thick.
Almost all of them carried on with no measurable deflection.
So almost all of the space they crossed contained nothing to deflect them: the atom is mostly empty.

items.objective_statement: relate the shell model of the atom to the periodic table
items.stem: The chemical properties of an element are decided mainly by the number of electrons in its

misconception.label: The inner shells are full and take no part in reactions.
The second shell matters only if it happens to be the outermost one.
The nucleus holds no electrons.

steps: Reactions involve electrons moving between atoms or being shared.
Only the outermost electrons are far enough from the nucleus to take part.
Elements with the same number of outer electrons appear in the same group of the periodic table and behave alike.

items.stem: Becquerel discovered radioactivity when he found that uranium salts

options.text: fogged a photographic plate wrapped in black paper

steps: Becquerel stored uranium salts beside a photographic plate wrapped in black paper.

options.text: the tube can be seen inside

steps: Radiation must get inside the tube to ionise the gas and produce a pulse.
Alpha particles are the least penetrating: a sheet of paper stops them.

items.objective_statement: recall that the decay process is independent of the conditions external to the nucleus
items.stem: A radioactive source is combined chemically into a new compound. Its half-life

misconception.label: Nothing available in a laboratory speeds decay up.
The source keeps decaying at exactly the same rate.
Nothing slows it down either.

steps: Chemical reactions rearrange the outer electrons of atoms.
Radioactive decay happens in the nucleus, deep inside and shielded by those electrons.
So temperature, pressure and chemical combination all leave the half-life untouched.
